stand: Russia and Ukraine continue exchanging long-range strikes. Zelensky says 78 were killed and 215 wounded across Ukraine in two days, after the Kramatorsk and Pryluky bombings. Putin told Trump that Ukrainian strikes during Russia's elections make an immediate resumption of peace talks unlikely; Witkoff and Kushner push new proposals and plan a Moscow visit this month. Kyiv is widening strikes to Russian AI data centres and missile plants. In Donetsk, Ukraine's Vivaldi offensive disputes Putin's claimed September gains. South Korea is recalling its Kyiv ambassador over a POW dispute.

Drones in Ukraine's overnight attack on Moscow region
Russia's oil refining capacity disabled (Ukraine's claim)
Economic cost of refinery strikes, acknowledged by Putin

src.name: President Vladimir Putin, Valdai Club forum (via ABC News)

claims.text: Russia says rail strikes hit military-logistics infrastructure, not civilians; Ukrainian accounts describe repeated strikes near passenger trains.
claims.by: Says: Russia's Defence Ministry — denies targeting civilians, says attacks target military transport infrastructure.

claims.text: Russia's Defence Ministry confirmed striking Kyiv's Northern Bridge, calling it a military-logistics target; two people were injured.
claims.by: Says: Russia's Defence Ministry, via Telegram — confirms the strike and its military rationale. Says: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko — two injured.

claims.text: Zelenskyy says Ukraine will intensify strikes on Russian oil refineries in retaliation for Russia's air campaign against Kyiv, and that Russian civilians will not be targeted.
claims.by: Says: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, to Reuters.

claims.text: Ukraine's Defence Ministry claims strikes have disabled 51% of Russia's oil refining capacity; the figure is unverified.
claims.by: Says: Ukraine Defence Ministry. Not independently verified — Russia has released no figures.

claims.text: Putin told Trump that Ukrainian drone strikes on Moscow during Russia's September elections make an immediate resumption of trilateral peace talks unlikely.
claims.by: Says: Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov, relaying the Trump-Putin call.

claims.text: Russian officials give fuller detail on the 650-drone Moscow-region attack: one killed in Radumlya, another in Barbybino, seven injured, 47 houses, four apartments and three cars damaged, and 185 drones destroyed or neutralised over the wider region.
claims.by: Says: Moscow Region Governor Andrei Vorobyov. No Ukrainian confirmation in sources reviewed.

claims.text: War blogger Yuri Podolyaka's claimed strike on the Volodarskaya oil facility concerns the largest such site in the Moscow region, linked to Transneft and Moscow's main refinery, supplying all three of the capital's airports; still no official confirmation.
claims.by: Says: war blogger Yuri Podolyaka. No official confirmation given.

claims.text: Estonia's Foreign Ministry says Russia is trying to intimidate foreign diplomats in Kyiv to undermine support for Ukraine; Estonia says its embassy is staying.
claims.by: Says: Estonian Foreign Ministry. No Russian response appears in sources reviewed.

claims.text: A Guardian investigation found sanctioned tankers carried South Korean fuel to Russia in July-August; an analyst says this undermines the sanctions regime, and Seoul did not address the shipments directly.
claims.by: Says: Guardian analysis / CREA analyst Isaac Levi. South Korea's foreign ministry did not address the shipments.

claims.text: India's external affairs minister says Delhi is becoming more actively involved in efforts to end the war, including on Black Sea shipping safety.
claims.by: Says: India's External Affairs Minister Jaishankar.

claims.text: Peace process: Ukraine has received four truce proposals — from India, Turkey, Egypt and the US — covering energy, ports and Black Sea shipping; India's is called the most comprehensive. The US-proposed trilateral meeting, once expected in early October, has slipped to late October, which Ukrainian officials blame on Russia; Russia reportedly rejected India's plan privately, unconfirmed publicly.
claims.by: Says: Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha; a Ukrainian official, via the Kyiv Independent. Says: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov — welcomes India's efforts but commits to nothing publicly.

claims.text: Russia's Defence Ministry says Geran attack drones struck several Ukrainian data centres (Parkovy, Ukrtelecom, Giga, Podolsky) that process data for government, commercial and military services.
claims.by: Says: Russia's Defence Ministry, via TASS.

claims.text: Ukraine's embassy in India accuses Russia of striking a factory owned by Indian investors, as Delhi shifts toward more active peacemaking.
claims.by: Says: Ukraine's embassy in India.

claims.text: Zelensky accuses Russia of deliberately targeting civilians with a strike timed as a 'birthday gift' for Putin, calling it an absolutely deliberate choice of terror.
claims.by: Says: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. No Russian response on the accusation in sources reviewed.

claims.text: Ukraine's air force says the overnight 6-7 October attack involved 130 drones, 48 cruise missiles and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles, with air defence downing 161 targets; Zelenskyy separately put the missile count at about 70, hitting eleven regions.
claims.by: Says: Ukraine's Air Force / President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

claims.text: Zelensky appeals to allies for US-made Patriot interceptors, saying Ukraine struggles to shoot down enemy ballistic missiles.
claims.by: Says: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

claims.text: Pryluky death toll: now confirmed at 22, including five children, with around 54 wounded, resolving earlier outlet disagreement (14 vs 18-22).
claims.by: Says: Chernihiv Governor Vyacheslav Chaus.

claims.text: A Russian strike causes a fire at a garage cooperative in Kyiv's Darnytskyi district, killing two people.
claims.by: Says: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko.

claims.text: Ukraine's air force intercepted over 80% of the 46 jet-powered drones launched, up from a recent average of 50-60%.
claims.by: Says: Ukraine's air force.

claims.text: Russia's Defence Ministry says its strike targeted military-industrial facilities including sites where Ukrainian firm Fire Point makes and stores Flamingo cruise missiles and long-range drones, across Kyiv, Chernihiv, Kirovohrad, Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava and Kharkiv regions, plus Odesa port infrastructure.
claims.by: Says: Russia's Defence Ministry. No Ukrainian confirmation of these specific targets in sources reviewed.

claims.text: Russian officials say naval drones hit a Liberian-flagged oil tanker near Sochi, with crude oil burning on the Black Sea; its Indian crew of 23 was rescued.
claims.by: Says: Russian officials.

claims.text: The search for sailors from the Black Sea grain ship that sank earlier this week has been called off with no survivors found; a second vessel was also hit in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone.
claims.by: Says: Bulgarian Vice-Admiral Rumen Nikolov; Says: Bulgarian PM Rumen Radev (on the second ship).

claims.text: WHO verified 180 attacks on healthcare in Ukraine in Q3 2026, a 17% rise on Q2, with 480 attacks verified in the first nine months of the year.
claims.by: Says: World Health Organization.

claims.text: Two WHO warehouses in Ukraine were hit in September: a main humanitarian warehouse in Kyiv region destroyed on 3 September and one in Chornomorsk damaged on 22 September, losing supplies meant for nearly 270,000 people.
claims.by: Says: World Health Organization.

claims.text: Kyiv's Dovzhenko Film Studio was damaged again in the strike, in a three-pavilion building; no fatalities reported.
claims.by: Says: Dovzhenko Film Studio, via Facebook.

claims.text: Zelenskyy calls the 7 October barrage one of the most vile strikes of the nearly five-year war.
claims.by: Says: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

claims.text: Ukraine's foreign minister Andrii Sybiha accuses Russian generals of giving Putin 'war crimes' as his birthday present, and says the fitting present would be a trial at The Hague.
claims.by: Says: Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha.

claims.text: Zelenskyy says Ukrainian forces struck four Russian targets in the past 24 hours: two oil facilities and a training ground in Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions, plus a response in the Black Sea.
claims.by: Says: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

claims.text: Turkish President Erdogan presses Putin on safe Black Sea navigation and repeats his offer to help facilitate direct Russia-Ukraine talks.
claims.by: Says: Turkish Presidency statement.

claims.text: WHO's new Winter Risk Assessment flags Sumy, Kharkiv, Chernihiv and Donetsk oblasts as facing the highest public-health risk this winter; separately, HeRAMS data show 629 of 11,099 tracked health facilities, or 6%, are non-operational, mostly in Donetska, Kharkivska, Sumska, Zaporizka and Poltavska oblasts.
claims.by: Says: World Health Organization.

claims.text: Ukraine's Air Force says Russia's monthly use of jet-powered attack drones rose from 350 in June to 3,500 in September, before easing to about 50 a night in October.
claims.by: Says: Ukrainian Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat.

claims.text: Russian state media TASS estimates Ukraine has lost more than $5bn in foreign-exchange revenue from the shutdown of Odesa-area ports, ongoing since 22 July.
claims.by: Says: TASS calculations.

claims.text: A Russian glide-bomb strike on two buses at a Kramatorsk bus stop killed at least 30 people and wounded 18; three more died in shelling nearby in Bilenke, and two more in an evening drone strike, taking the city's Thursday toll to 35.
claims.by: Says: Donetsk regional prosecutor's office; Kramatorsk City Council, via Telegram.

claims.text: Ukrainian officials accuse Russia of deliberately targeting a civilian bus stop to kill as many people as possible; Russia has not commented on the strike.
claims.by: Says: Donetsk Governor Vadym Filashkin; President Volodymyr Zelensky. No Russian comment in sources reviewed.

claims.text: Seoul says Ukraine broke a confidentiality agreement on the POW transfer and is owed an apology; Kyiv denies any such agreement existed.
claims.by: Says: South Korea's government — Ukraine breached a non-disclosure agreement. Denies: Ukraine's Foreign Ministry — no non-disclosure agreement existed.

claims.text: South Korea's Foreign Ministry says it has decided to recall its ambassador to Ukraine, Park Hee-chang, over the POW dispute.
claims.by: Says: South Korea's Foreign Ministry.

claims.text: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Russia's war on Ukraine is at a dangerous stalemate, and Washington remains committed to pursuing a negotiated settlement.
claims.by: Says: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

claims.text: A second Ukrainian strike in as many days partly disabled Yandex's Kaluga data centre, after an earlier attack took its Ryazan AI-supercomputer hub offline; Kyiv is widening its campaign to Russia's AI infrastructure.
claims.by: Says: Yandex, company statement.

claims.text: Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck a large oil refinery and petrochemical complex in Salavat, Russia, about 1,200km east of Moscow; the claim is unverified.
claims.by: Says: Ukraine's General Staff. Not independently verified.

claims.text: Zelensky urged the US to expand Starlink satellite coverage so Ukraine could strike launch sites inside Russia; Trump and Musk have so far refused.
claims.by: Says: President Volodymyr Zelensky. Trump and Musk have not granted the request, per Guardian reporting.

claims.text: Trump announced that Russia agreed to deliver more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel to American and global markets, a deal Zelensky called a gift to Putin.
claims.by: Says: US President Donald Trump. Says: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy — calls it a gift to Putin funding the war against Ukraine.

claims.text: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner are pushing new proposals to end the war, presented to Trump and UK, French and German security advisers plus NATO/EU officials, and plan to visit Moscow this month.
claims.by: Says: Axios, citing American and Ukrainian sources.

claims.text: The US-mediated Washington talks on 9-10 October will cover security guarantees for Ukraine and a postwar reconstruction plan, broader than earlier reports of air-defence talks alone, with a European team also joining.
claims.by: Says: unnamed US officials, per AFP (via Tagesschau).

claims.text: Zelensky says 78 people were killed and 215 wounded in Russian attacks across Ukraine over the two days before 9 October.
claims.by: Says: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

claims.text: Ukraine's military says it struck a missile-component factory in Tver region, an ICBM-disassembly centre in Nizhny Novgorod, and the Ukhta oil refinery 1,900km inside Russia.
claims.by: Says: Ukraine's General Staff; President Volodymyr Zelenskyy (Ukhta refinery). Not independently verified.

claims.text: Putin claims Russia captured 1,300 sq km of Ukraine in September; an independent monitor says Russia actually lost around 80 sq km that month, as Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi reclaims ground near Lyman.
claims.by: Says: President Vladimir Putin — Russia gained 1,300 sq km in September. Denies: Institute for the Study of War — found Russia lost territory that month, using geolocated open-source data.

claims.text: Ukraine's military says Russian casualties hit a 2026 monthly record of 46,230 in September, with more than 70% confirmed kills, and that total Russian dead and wounded since 2022 reached 1,545,950 by 7 October.
claims.by: Says: Ukraine's military / General Staff. No independent verification in sources reviewed.

claims.text: Germany's foreign minister accuses Putin of boundless cruelty over recent civilian strikes and says Berlin will significantly tighten sanctions on Russia's war economy and its backers.
claims.by: Says: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul.

claims.text: A Ukrainian attack on Russia's Belgorod region killed two people and wounded twelve, regional officials said.
claims.by: Says: Belgorod regional emergency headquarters; Governor Alexander Shuvayev.

claims.text: A Ukrainian drone attack wounded nine people in Russia's Kaluga region, the regional governor said.
claims.by: Says: Kaluga Governor Vladislav Shapsha.

timeline.text: Drone strike near an Odesa-Kirovohrad passenger train forces a trackside evacuation; the train itself was not damaged.
A relative lull in large Ukrainian drone strikes on the Moscow region begins.
Putin says Ukrainian refinery strikes have cost Russia about 1% of GDP.
Russian drone strikes Kyiv's Northern Bridge over the Dnipro, damaging the road surface and injuring two.
Russia's Defence Ministry confirms the Northern Bridge strike via Telegram, calling Zelenskyy responsible for the escalation.
German Chancellor Merz visits Kyiv, pledging €1bn in military aid.
Russian drone attack injures a 53-year-old man in Pryozerne, Kherson region; separate shelling injures a woman in Bilozerka.
Russia launches 205 drones overnight into Monday; Ukraine's air force says 172 are shot down or suppressed.
Russian guided aerial bomb attack kills at least three and wounds 39 in Kharkiv; a search for people under rubble is under way.
Russian drone attack sinks a Turkish-owned grain ship in Romania's Black Sea waters; two killed, 11 rescued.
German minister Karin Prien arrives in Kyiv, a day after Merz's visit, to highlight support for children and civil society.
Russia says it struck the port of Vylkove and fuel depots at Chornomorsk in Odesa region and a power plant in Kharkiv region; one dead, six injured in Kharkiv.
Estonia's embassy says it is staying in Kyiv despite Russian intimidation; Ukraine's foreign ministry had denied reports of Western embassies evacuating west.
Ukraine strikes Russia's Moscow region overnight with roughly 650 drones; Russian officials say two are killed and a warehouse set ablaze.
A separate Ukrainian drone attack hits a minibus in Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia, killing three, Moscow-installed officials say.
Casualties from the Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia's Dnipro bridge rise to five injured, including two Red Cross workers.
A Russian drone strike sparks a fire on the roof of an educational institution in Kyiv's Obolon district; no casualties, fire extinguished.
Russian forces strike infrastructure in Odesa region again overnight; no casualties, residential areas undamaged.
Dutch PM Rob Jetten pledges F-16 maintenance, spare parts and ammunition for Ukraine after talks with Zelenskyy on air defence.
Russia's Defence Ministry says its Geran drones struck Ukrainian data centres used by government, commercial and military services.
Russian forces strike a warehouse facility in Zaporizhzhia, killing a man.
Ukraine's air force detects three Tu-160 strategic bombers taking off from Russia's Belaya airfield, hours before the mass missile-and-drone barrage.
Russia fires roughly 70 missiles, many ballistic, and 46 jet-powered drones at Ukraine overnight, hitting eleven regions on Putin's birthday.
A fire at a garage cooperative in Kyiv's Darnytskyi district kills two people.
Russia's Defence Ministry says it struck Ukrainian military-industrial sites, including Fire Point's missile facilities and Odesa port infrastructure.
An oil tanker burns near Sochi after Russian officials report a naval drone strike; its Indian crew of 23 is rescued.
The search for sailors from the Black Sea grain ship that sank earlier this week is called off with no survivors found.
A Russian missile destroys a five-storey apartment block in Pryluky; the death toll later rises to 22, including five children, with around 54 wounded.
Merz visits Kyiv again, announcing a 1.3bn-euro military aid package and signing agreements worth 8.5bn euros.
Russian guided aerial bombs strike the 'Intellect' gymnasium in Kushuhum, Zaporizhzhia region, for a second time, causing significant damage.
A Russian drone strikes a 12-storey residential building in Kyiv's Desnianskyi district; 22 people including 8 children are rescued and four injured.
A Russian glide bomb hits two civilian buses at a stop in Kramatorsk, killing at least 30 and wounding 18; all public transport in the city is suspended.
Shelling kills three more people in Bilenke, near Kramatorsk, and an evening drone strike kills two more in the city, raising Kramatorsk's Thursday toll to 35.
South Korea's Foreign Ministry announces it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine, Park Hee-chang, over the North Korean POW transfer dispute.
A Ukrainian drone attack damages a Yandex data centre in Russia's Ryazan region, knocking some Russian websites offline.
Ukraine says it struck a major oil refinery complex in Salavat, Russia, and that Ukrainian drones reached Russia's Omsk region, more than 2,000km from the border.
Kyiv's grid operator Ukrenergo orders emergency power outages as Russian strikes worsen blackouts; water pressure drops and the metro briefly halts all trains.
Kyiv police defuse two unexploded half-ton ballistic missile warheads that landed near residential buildings.
Zelensky accuses the US of being unwilling to help Ukraine, criticising Washington's pursuit of economic ties with Russia alongside mediation efforts.
The UK opens its first dedicated industry business centre in Kyiv, the Kyiv Business Centre, to deepen UK-Ukraine defence-industrial ties.
Lithuania deploys about 100 additional troops to its border with Russia's Kaliningrad enclave.
Witkoff and Kushner present new proposals to end the war to Trump at the White House, with UK, French and German security advisers and NATO/EU representatives attending.
A Ukrainian delegation is due to meet US officials Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff for two days to discuss strengthening Ukraine's air defences.
Putin tells Trump by phone that Ukrainian drone strikes during Russia's elections make an immediate resumption of peace talks unlikely.
Trump announces Russia will deliver over 300,000 tonnes of diesel to US and global markets; Zelensky calls it a gift to Putin.
Ukrainian drones partly disable Yandex's Kaluga data centre, a day after knocking its Ryazan AI-supercomputer hub offline.
Zelensky says Russian attacks killed 78 people and wounded 215 across Ukraine over the preceding two days.
Ukraine's military says it struck Russian missile-production sites in Tver and Nizhny Novgorod regions and the Ukhta oil refinery, 1,900km from the border.
German Foreign Minister Wadephul accuses Putin of boundless cruelty and vows tougher EU sanctions on Russia's war economy.

headline: Putin rules out quick peace talks as strikes hit Russian AI hubs
